subject: Integrated lighting and accessory storage
hook: The neatest wardrobe lighting starts as a hole you'll never see.
ig:
The neatest wardrobe lighting starts as a hole you'll never see.

When lighting is planned in from the start, the work happens in the workshop before the wardrobe is assembled:

Cable routes are drilled to the drawing, so wiring runs inside the carcass rather than along the outside.

Panels can be grooved to take a light profile flush, instead of a strip stuck on later.

Accessory drawers are cut, edged and assembled with dividers for watches, jewellery and belts.

Everything is checked against the plan before it leaves Hanley, and a qualified electrician connects the lighting on site.

This is the difference between lighting that looks designed in and lighting that looks added after.

If you're planning a wardrobe with lights, DM us and tell us where the nearest socket or supply is. It helps us plan the route.
fb:
A little behind-the-scenes from the workshop: this is where wardrobe lighting really starts.

Cable holes drilled to the drawing, grooves machined so the light sits flush, and accessory drawers built with dividers, all before the wardrobe is assembled. On site, a qualified electrician connects it up, and the result looks like it was always meant to be there.

Have a look at our fitted wardrobes if you're planning one with lights.
